correctness.rationale: The piecewise exponential profile gives exactly W(a)=min(max(a,1),1/q)*max(1,d-(1-q)a). The entire compact interval 0<=a<=d is partitioned at first-dose threshold 1, retained threshold 1/q and post-second threshold (d-1)/(1-q). Only the strictly concave quadratic a(d-(1-q)a) and the strictly decreasing cap can outperform a single bolus; comparing the vertex, cap, endpoints and all equality boundaries proves the complete real-parameter optimizer set. The half-life switch q=1/2, d=4(1-q) jump and strict equal-split inversion are analytically derived. A standalone exact-rational checker passed 183183 assertions over 5200 randomized and dedicated boundary parameter cases, only as corroboration. Infinite-domain claims rest on algebraic proof, not these samples.

value.rationale: Time above MIC is a longstanding pharmacodynamic exposure quantity, and a fixed total dose with two prescribed delivery times is a natural minimal model of fractionation. The analysis exposes an exact one-half-life boundary between first-order continuous and discontinuous emergence of a beneficial second bolus, two sharp budget thresholds, and a nonempty open region where equal splitting is strictly worse than giving all at once while an unequal split is strictly superior. This furnishes a meaningful structural counterexample to a natural equal-fractionation heuristic, not just an arbitrary numerical parameter evaluation. Real prescribing applications require separate clinical modeling and validation.
